Article Title: Major accident averted as empty Vande Bharat travels 463 km with faulty brakes
Article Text:
The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi

NEW DELHI: A major accident was averted after an empty Vande Bharat train travelled nearly 463 km with its coaches' braking systems allegedly non-functional, despite repeated warnings from loco pilots. The incident, which took place in October, has prompted the South Eastern Railway (SER) zone to order a probe into multiple safety lapses that could have endangered railway operations.The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh using a freight locomotive. According to PTI, railway staff failed to properly integrate the train's braking system with the locomotive and ignored warnings from the crew before allowing it to continue its journey.The incident came days before the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailment in Assam on November 11, which also raised concerns over alleged negligence in railway operations.In an order dated November 7, the SER zone directed the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Ranchi to investigate the incident and identify those responsible.According to the order, the loco pilot conducted a brake power test after departing from Hatia and found that the braking performance was extremely poor.He submitted a written complaint to railway officials upon reaching Ranchi, but the train was allowed to proceed.Another loco pilot operating the rake from Muri station also alerted the concerned controllers, reporting that the brakes could not be applied by dropping the brake pipe (BP) pressure.It was only when the train reached Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) station in Uttar Pradesh's Chandauli district that officials inspected the rake. They found that the braking systems of all coaches had been isolated, rendering them ineffective.The preliminary probe identified alleged negligence by coach and wagon maintenance staff, section and traction controllers, as well as the train crew. It noted that maintenance staff had failed to physically verify the brakes before departure, while the crew's unfamiliarity with the Vande Bharat's braking system also contributed to the lapse.
Article Summary: The incident occurred on October 24, when an empty Vande Bharat chair car rake was being transported from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh. South Eastern Railway (SER) zone has ordered a probe into multiple safety lapses that could have endangered railway operations.

Article Title: Faith, pollution and politics: How Yamuna takes centre stage every Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Significance of Chhath

Chhath and politics go hand in hand in Delhi

Why Chhath has become a political event

Why the Yamuna turns frothy around Chhath

The health risks for the devotees

NEW DELHI: Purity, hygiene and cleanliness are paramount for devotees during Chhath Puja . With God as their witness - quite literally in this case - devotees go to great lengths to observe strict hygiene while following elaborate rituals centred around the worship of the Sun deity over four days.In Delhi, however, devotees will step into the sullied waters of the Yamuna, believing that their faith will protect them.As Delhi is already gasping for breath after Diwali, the debate has now pivoted to the pollution of the river which Delhi, for most of the year, views from the bridges built over it.As thousands of people come down to the Yamuna's banks, the river will undergo its annual public audit by devotees standing waist-deep in its waters.Chhath Puja, rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand.Observed over four days, the festival begins with Nahay-Khay, when devotees prepare simple, traditional food while observing strict personal hygiene and purity.This is followed by Kharna, when jaggery-based kheer and wheat rotis are prepared as prasad.After Kharna, devotees undertake a rigorous 36-hour nirjala fast, abstaining from both food and water.The rituals culminate in offerings of arghya to the setting Sun, followed by prayers to the rising Sun on the final day.Every year, as Chhath Puja approaches, the Yamuna becomes more than a river for Delhi.This year, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari took a dip in the Yamuna at Sonia Vihar, praising the cleanup under chief minister Rekha Gupta.“How can we not appreciate the work that has been done here?” he said. “There might be crocodiles in the water here, but crocodiles come in clean water.”AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar answered by floating an effigy of Tiwari at Kalindi Kunj and challenging him to bathe there, claiming that stretch was far more polluted.On Nahay Khay, the first day of the festival, a video purportedly showing dead fish near Sonia Vihar surfaced on social media.Delhi ministers accused AAP of staging it, alleging that party workers bought fish from the market and dumped them in the river.Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj denied this and demanded an inquiry on Friday, saying water samples had not yet been collected to establish the cause.The river has been a political flashpoint around Chhath before. Last year, AAP alleged that a temporary artificial pool at Vasudev Ghat was built to project a clean Yamuna ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s planned Chhath visit, which did not take place.Chhath's growing political importance has a lot to do with Delhi's changing demography. According to reports, continued migration from Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP has increased the share of the Purvanchali community to about 30 percent of Delhi's population.The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency through a celebration deeply woven into its cultural identity.According to reports, the Delhi government is setting up 1,482 Chhath ghats across 996 locations. The growing prominence of a festival once largely observed within community networks reflects how it has become an important fixture on the capital's political calendar.The Yamuna's pollution becomes particularly visible around Chhath Puja, when devotees gather in large numbers along its banks to offer prayers.While talking to the Times of India, environmentalist Saumya Dutta said that the timing of Chhath coincides with a period when the river's flow has receded considerably after the monsoon, leaving less water to dilute the pollutants entering it.“During the days of Chhath Puja, tens of thousands of Delhi residents from Bihar and eastern UP, along with others, add huge amounts of pollutants, particularly detergents containing surfactants, which are common ingredients in soaps and detergents, as well as some industrial waste,” Dutta said.“Long after the peak monsoon flow, this is the period when the Yamuna's flow becomes very low. This low water flow, combined with high amounts of surfactants, causes large amounts of foam when the water is agitated. This becomes particularly visible during the huge influx of people and pollutants into this short 2% stretch of the Yamuna,” he said.According to Dutta, the 22-km stretch through the capital accounts for roughly 2% of the Yamuna's total length but contributes 70-80% of its overall pollution load.“Defaming agents and pre-Chhath cleaning do help for a very short period, but as the incoming pollution does not go down, this benefit is very short-term and vanishes quickly,” Dutta told TOI.“The major reason for the abject failure of Yamuna cleaning plans, as well as schemes like Namami Gange, is that the huge daily inflow of partially treated or even untreated sewage and industrial effluent into the river is not being tackled,” he added.In one of the most polluted major rivers of India, devotees will stand waist-deep, waiting for the Sun to set and rise the following day.But is it safe for a person to come in contact with such polluted river?According to Dr Srijan Garg immersion during Chhath can expose people to harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites through the skin, eyes, nose and ears, and sometimes through accidental ingestion."Devotees are exposed through the skin, eyes, nose, ear and sometimes by ingestion. However, the major exposure is through the skin and can cause various infections such as folliculitis, dermatitis, fungal infections," Dr. Garg told TOI.The water is full of untreated sewage water. so swallowing that water will affect the health of the individual. Some acute infections typhoid, hepatitis A or E, giardiasis, cholera. These usually present with diarrhoea, vomiting and pain abdomen," he added.Meanwhile, Dr. Ishan Singh said that people with cuts or open wounds are particularly vulnerable to infections."Industrial discharge may introduce heavy metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium into river water. Depending on concentration and duration of exposure, these can affect the kidneys, liver and nervous system. Some chemicals may also irritate the skin and eyes," Dr. Singh told TOI."However, their actual presence and concentration at individual ghats must be confirmed through laboratory testing. A single brief exposure should not automatically be considered a cause of heavy-metal poisoning," he added.He also said that children, pregnant women, elderly people, diabetic patients and people with weakened immunity need particular attention.Dr. Singh also advised devotees to avoid swallowing river water, keep immersion time short and stay away from areas close to sewage discharge points. Those with open wounds should preferably avoid entering the water. After immersion, devotees should wash thoroughly with clean water and soap and change out of wet clothes.Chhath will end with prayers to the rising Sun, as devotees complete the four-day rituals with hopes and gratitude. However, the Yamuna's problems will remain long after the devotees leave the ghats.The wait for a cleaner river is likely to continue, with sewage and industrial waste flowing into it despite periodic cleaning drives and political promises.And when Chhath returns next year, the river will once again face its annual public audit, with the same questions over its cleanliness and safety likely to resurface.
Article Summary: Chhath Puja is rooted in devotion to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya. It is primarily observed by people from Bihar, eastern UP and Jharkhand. The festival offers political parties an opportunity to reach a sizeable constituency.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday renewed his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a one-on-one public debate, claiming that the prime minister would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange.During an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram, the Congress MP was asked why he continued to insist on a public debate when the BJP had said the discussion could take place in Parliament.The leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha said he was not allowed to speak freely in the House and alleged that his microphone had been switched off."You did not let me talk on the farm bills, vote chori, SIR, China, on (Gen) Naravane's book, Epstein. I want a one-on-one debate. I don't want a debate entailing long speeches," he said.The Raebareli MP proposed a direct exchange in which both leaders could make allegations against each other, rather than deliver lengthy speeches."I want that Narendra Modi makes allegations against me and I do the same to him. He can come; there will be a table, on one side there will be Narendra Modi ji and on the other side, it would be me," he said.He added that he would have no objection if Adani Group chairperson Gautam Adani or Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat was appointed to judge the debate."But I guarantee that the prime minister will not remain the PM after a one-on-one debate with me," Rahul said.He also alleged that PM Modi is anti-national and is controlled by foreign powers.Responding to a question regarding proof of such foreign aid allegations, he said, “The proof is here. It's in this phone. The Prime Minister knows it because he taps my phone. The moment he comes for the debate, one-on-one debate, everybody will know who's controlled by foreign powers, who's an anti-national, since when he's been an anti-national, and lots of other details that I know and I wrote on my phone.”The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate. He had earlier claimed that it would take him just five minutes to establish that the prime minister was a "traitor".In a series of posts and videos shared on X last week, Rahul also challenged PM Modi to debate allegations concerning foreign influence, national security and who was anti-national.In one video, he said 24 hours had passed since he first issued the challenge and urged the prime minister to choose any venue. He proposed that the discussion take place in front of the media and the country's youth, with both leaders seated across a table and PM Modi choosing the moderator or judge. Rahul had suggested Bhagwat for the role.In another post, former Congress president renewed the challenge while responding to PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks. Addressing CRPF personnel who had attended the prime minister's Diwali event in Bastar, he claimed their expressions suggested they did not agree with PM Modi's comments."Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals," Gandhi wrote.He also said the debate should address who was anti-national and who was controlled by foreign forces.BJP leaders have scoffed at Rahul's repeated calls for a debate, alleging that he has avoided discussions in Parliament.Union home minister Amit Shah has challenged Rahul to debate him in Parliament, asking him to bring his allegations and arguments to the House instead of taking political debate to the streets."If you (Rahul Gandhi) wish to engage in a responsible discussion—if your concerns hold truth, substance, and logic—then come and discuss them inside Parliament. Let’s face each other head-on! But you won’t be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away," Shah said at a rally in Karnal, Haryana.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has also said that Parliament already provides a platform for such an exchange and urged the Congress MP to show "some seriousness and responsibility" in his role as the leader of the opposition.Rahul's latest remarks come amid the continuing political exchange between the Congress and the BJP over his allegations against Modi and the prime minister's criticism of the opposition.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi renews his challenge to PM Modi for a one-on-one public debate. He claims PM Modi would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange. The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate.

Article Title: Air India Delhi-SFO was 2.5 hours away from destination when US ATC failed; all 5 AI flights landed on time
Article Text:
All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time

Poll Vote & Share your view How concerned are you about air travel disruptions due to ground stops? Very concerned Somewhat concerned Not very concerned Not concerned at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Air India ’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination, when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th when Uncle Sam’s outdated air traffic control (ATC) systems began to fail. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. Luckily, the US Air Traffic Control System Command Centre (ATCSCC) advisory issued at 2.24 am (IST of Nov 14) to announce the ground stop said “inbound international flights will be managed on a case by case basis” while asking all departing flights to remain on ground. The Boeing 777 (VT-ALS) landed in SFO at 5 am.“As soon as the ATCSCC advisory was issued at 2.24 am, AI flight operations buzzed the leadership team and they went into a huddle. SFO flight was the closest to its destination and proceeded since the pilots, who were in touch with Oakland control at that time, were not told to divert as per the advisory which meant the B777 will be allowed to land,” said people in the know.AI kept a close eye on the developing situation and the four other flights — one each from Delhi and Mumbai to Newark (EWR) and JFK — kept proceeding to their destinations.The outage lasted about five hours and these all landed as per schedule.Of the five return flights these aircraft were to operate back home, only SFO-Delhi (via Kolkata) was delayed by about 2 hours and 40 minutes due to congestion at SFO. “All the other flights, two each out of EWR and JFK, operated on time,” said an official, adding Saturday-Sunday night departures were also on time except for the delayed arrival from SFO.AI senior pilots said this is the second time in less than four years that US faced an air traffic communication issue, although Friday the 13th was by far the most serious one. On Jan 10, 2023, the US Federal Aviation Administration was unable to issue notice to airmen (NOTAM) for some hours and it had to activate a hotline to manage the situation then. The FAA subsequently traced the problem to files unintentionally deleted by contract personnel while correcting synchronisation between the primary and backup databases.Following Friday’s failure, the US is prioritising international flights over domestic ones and the situation will take some days to recover as there will be a serious ripple effect. While Air India is the only Indian operator that flies to the US, two US carriers — United and American — have a daily each between Delhi and New York. Rest of the connectivity is provided by onestops of Gulf, European and southeast Asian carriers.Other airlines’ flights were also impacted.“Given the scale of the failure, the impact was massive. I was listening to ground control at JFK when the issue happened just before 4 pm EST (New York time) Friday. There were a lot of frustrated pilots and controllers. Hundreds of pilots were asking, ‘what’s the delay reason,’. Initially controller couldn’t give a reason and just said, ‘nationwide stop.’ Later it was determined a communication problem,” said a pilot who was in New York at that time.“Due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety, attention all aircraft operators: By order of the Federal Aviation Command Centre, all airports are ground stopped,” the ATCSCC advisory announcing the failure had said.
Article Summary: Air India’s Delhi-San Francisco (SFO) nonstop was over the Pacific and just about two hours away from its destination when the US ordered a ground stop on Friday the 13th. There were four other AI nonstops, all to New York via the Atlantic route, but they were further away from their destinations. All 5 AI flights landed safely at their destinations and on time.

Article Title: Studying abroad, visiting India or working overseas? Who gets counted in Census 2027 across UP
Article Text:
Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas.

LUCKNOW: Indian residents travelling abroad temporarily will be counted at their usual place of residence if they return during the 35-day enumeration period of Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, subject to enumeration rules.The clarification comes ahead of the 15-day online self-enumeration exercise in Uttar Pradesh, beginning Nov 16 and continuing until Nov 30, followed by door-to-door population enumeration from Dec 1, 2026, to Jan 4, 2027.Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas.Indian citizens studying, working or permanently residing abroad throughout the enumeration period would generally not be included in their family's household merely because they hold Indian passports.Parents completing online self-enumeration should therefore not include children ordinarily residing abroad.However, if a temporarily absent family member returns during the enumeration period and qualifies for inclusion, the enumerator can update the household details during the physical visit.Personnel posted at Indian diplomatic missions abroad will be covered through special arrangements coordinated centrally.Conversely, foreign nationals ordinarily residing in India, including students and workers, will be counted irrespective of citizenship. Short-term foreign visitors and diplomatic personnel enjoying immunity are subject to separate rules.Verma emphasised that the census records population, not citizenship, and inclusion does not confer Indian citizenship.Similarly, seasonal migrant workers residing in Uttar Pradesh during enumeration, including those employed at brick kilns, sugar mills and other establishments, will be counted in the state.They should inform enumerators at their places of origin to prevent duplication.The census reference time is midnight at the start of Jan 5, 2027. A revisional round from January 5 to 9 will account for births, deaths and omissions.Final census data is scheduled to be made public in April 2027.
Article Summary: Sheetal Verma, director of census operations and chief principal census officer, Uttar Pradesh, explained that temporary absence from India was different from ordinarily residing overseas. The clarification comes ahead of the 15-day online self-enumeration exercise in Uttar Pradesh.

NEW DELHI: India's border with China has become "more alive" and requires a much greater commitment of Indian troops on a sustained basis, EAM S Jaishankar said Saturday as he listed New Delhi's policy approach to enhance infrastructure along the frontier.Jaishankar also said that India has bolstered its military capabilities along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) since the deadly clashes in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020.His remarks came amid ongoing efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to normalise ties that came under severe strain following the over four-year border face-off in eastern Ladakh."Just think about the last few years. How often do you now read - a new tunnel has been built, some new bridge has been built, another airfield has been commissioned. You're getting this news with greater and greater frequency," he said."What has happened today is the border with China has become more alive in a way. It has required a much greater commitment of troops on a sustained basis."After over four years of frosty ties over the eastern Ladakh military standoff, India and China began to repair relations following a meeting between PM Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Russian city of Kazan in Oct 2024."I would say when it comes to the border, I would honestly make this point, and I think there's a lot of data and evidence to back it up, which is that the border infrastructure was really neglected till about a decade ago. I mean, people spoke about it, people drew up plan," Jaishankar said.He added India's capability to "deploy" its troops on that border has seen "a very marked" improvement.He also responded to a question on views about economic asymmetry between the two countries. "Remember, when around the time when Rajiv Gandhi went to China in 1988, the Indian and Chinese economies were about the same size," he said. "...China, in the 1980s particularly, made a huge push towards modernisation and industrialisation. India in the 1980s simply missed the bus. Now, in the 1990s, we did some corrections, reforms, but we did not carry through the reforms sector by sector and keep building and raising it," he said."I don't want you to think of it as a political point," he said and listed efforts by the Modi govt in the areas of manufacturing and industrialisation.
Article Summary: Jaishankar says India has bolstered its military capabilities along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) since deadly clashes in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020. His remarks came amid ongoing efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to normalise ties that came under severe strain following the over four-year border face-off.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Current world No. 1 Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend over domestic abuse allegations ahead of ATP finals
Article Text:
Alexander Zverev (Reuters Photo)

Brenda Patea sues Alexander Zverev over claims his innocence was proven

Why Alexander Zverev’s original domestic abuse case ended without a verdict

Zverev faces renewed scrutiny as he prepares for ATP Finals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alexander Zverev will begin his bid for a third ATP Finals title under renewed legal scrutiny after his former partner, Brenda Patea, filed a civil lawsuit over his public statements about the domestic abuse case she brought against him. The action, lodged in Berlin, challenges his claims that the allegations were disproved and that his innocence had been established, despite the earlier proceedings ending without a verdict.The lawsuit was filed on September 18, with Patea, the mother of Zverev’s five-year-old daughter, seeking legal action over comments the German tennis player made after criminal proceedings relating to her allegations were discontinued in June 2024.The case centres on Zverev’s repeated assertions that the allegations had been proven false and that his innocence had been established. Patea argues that those statements misrepresented the outcome of the proceedings and breached an agreement reached when the original case was settled.According to tennis journalist Ben Rothenberg, who first reported the new action for Bounces , Patea’s legal representatives had previously written to Zverev asking him to stop making such statements.The lawsuit says that he did not respond. Her lawyer, Michael Scheele, said the action was intended both to seek redress for his client and to prevent further statements of the same nature.“This lawsuit serves both to provide satisfaction to the plaintiff and to prevent further infringements,” Scheele said.He argued that Zverev’s comments had caused particular harm because they were made to an international publication and subsequently repeated by German media.“In the present case, a serious infringement has occurred,” Scheele said. “The defendant made a false factual assertion to an international newspaper that his innocence had been proven. This statement was disseminated internationally and picked up by numerous German media outlets.“It discredits the plaintiff as a liar and portrays her as a person who wrongfully accused the defendant. Furthermore, the defendant has breached a contractual obligation to refrain from such conduct, which makes the motive and degree of his fault particularly egregious.”The lawsuit seeks compensation for damage to Patea’s public standing, alongside an injunction intended to prevent further statements. She had initially applied for a preliminary injunction, but withdrew that application on September 14 before filing the claim four days later.The Berlin court has assigned the case a number and issued a procedural order dated November 5. However, the lawsuit had not yet been formally served on Zverev at the time of the reports. The action therefore represents a new civil dispute over his public comments, rather than a reopening of the criminal proceedings that ended in 2024.The lawsuit also sets out why Patea had previously hesitated to pursue Zverev through the courts. It says she feared reprisals from him and anticipated that he would be less willing to reach an out-of-court agreement over the child support she was seeking.The dispute stems from allegations made by Patea about an incident in Berlin in May 2020. She accused Zverev of pushing her against a wall and strangling her with both hands during an argument. Patea had made her allegations public, and Zverev has consistently denied them.On October 2, 2023, Berlin’s Tiergarten district court issued a penalty order against the tennis player, imposing a €450,000 fine. The amount was calculated through 90 daily payments of €5,000. Zverev challenged the order, preventing it from becoming final and leading to a criminal trial in 2024.Proceedings began in May that year, while Zverev was competing at the French Open, where he reached the final. The case was discontinued in June after an agreement was reached between Zverev, Patea and the prosecution.Under the settlement, Zverev agreed to pay €200,000, comprising €150,000 to the state and €50,000 to charitable organisations. Crucially, the proceedings ended without a finding of guilt or innocence, and Zverev did not admit to the allegations.The distinction became central to the statements that have now prompted Patea’s civil action. After the proceedings were discontinued, Zverev suggested during a press conference at Roland Garros that the decision itself demonstrated his innocence.“They’re not going to drop the case if you’re guilty at the end of the day. I don’t know what translations you have, but that’s what it means. Done. We move on. I never ever want to hear another question about the subject again. That goes out to everybody,” he said.He returned to the subject in a June 2025 interview with L’Équipe , conducted the morning after winning his maiden Grand Slam title at the French Open. Asked about the allegations by journalist Quentin Moynet, Zverev challenged the premise of the question.“First of all, this isn’t that kind of interview. Secondly, you know that the accusations have been proven false?” he said.When the journalist argued that the allegations remained a legitimate subject of discussion, Zverev added: “I did everything I could, and my innocence has been proven.”Patea’s new lawsuit challenges precisely that interpretation of the outcome. The criminal proceedings were discontinued following a settlement, but there was no trial verdict establishing that the allegations were false or that Zverev had been cleared.The lawsuit arrives at a significant moment in Zverev’s career. The German has risen to world No. 1 and secured the year-end top ranking for 2026, and is preparing to compete at the ATP Finals in Turin, where the tournament begins on Sunday. He will be seeking a third title at the season-ending championship.The new legal action is not the first time Zverev has faced allegations of abuse involving a former partner. Olya Sharypova, another former girlfriend and a former tennis player, made allegations against him in October 2020, describing incidents of alleged physical and emotional abuse during their relationship in 2019. She said some of the incidents occurred in cities where ATP tournaments were being held.Zverev denied Sharypova’s allegations. The ATP opened an investigation that lasted 15 months before announcing in January 2023 that it would take no disciplinary action, citing insufficient evidence to substantiate the claims.That investigation was separate from the criminal proceedings brought by Patea in Germany. The ATP’s decision concerned whether there was sufficient evidence for disciplinary action under its own rules; the Berlin case involved allegations examined through the German criminal justice system.Zverev has denied the allegations made by both women. The new lawsuit does not establish liability, and its claims will have to be considered through the civil proceedings. It does, however, bring his public account of the Patea case back into focus just as he prepares for one of the biggest tournaments of his season.
Article Summary: Brenda Patea sues Alexander Zverev over claims his innocence was proven. The action, lodged in Berlin, challenges his claims that the allegations were disproved and that his innocence had been established. The dispute stems from allegations made by PateA about an incident in Berlin in May 2020.

Article Title: Auston Matthews' postgame comments put Jim Hiller under scrutiny as Toronto Maple Leafs search for answers amid NHL struggles

What needs to change for Toronto Maple Leafs?

The Toronto Maple Leafs are facing some criticism after one win in their last eight games and questions about the direction of the team and coaching style. And then there’s the communication and the accountability within the organization. That was touched on some more by captain Auston Matthews, who said head coach Jim Hiller typically doesn’t talk to players postgame.Matthews’ comments have resonated with Toronto fans, especially as the team looks to regain its consistency. But as the criticism mounts, there are still questions about whether it’s fair to judge Hiller’s early tenure so quickly.Auston Matthews’ comments have shone a light on Jim Hiller’s communication style as the Toronto Maple Leafs look to snap out of their recent stretch of poor results.Generally, Hiller doesn’t talk to the players after the game, Matthews said, but that was after another loss. Instead, the Toronto captain said the team will concentrate on watching video, fixing mistakes and making adjustments.Matthews said Hiller is usually quiet after games, and said the players will continue to work on fixing their mistakes.He also stressed the importance of minimising turnovers, particularly against the opponent’s top lines.These mistakes can lead to scoring chances for the other team and put pressure on the Toronto defence.The response from Toronto Maple Leafs fans was mostly critical, with many questioning whether Hiller's approach has enough communication and accountability during a tough stretch.Sports broadcaster Sid Seixeiro expressed dire concerns about the situation, saying Toronto has to take care of its issues before the season gets even further away from them.NHL insider Chris Johnston says talk about Hiller being on the hot seat is overblown.Johnston said he didn't think credible sources were seriously expecting Toronto to fire Hiller after about 20 games in charge.That assessment is key context to the growing speculation. The Maple Leafs are having a disappointing season, but a short stretch of poor results does not necessarily mean management has decided to replace its head coach.The Toronto Maple Leafs’ problems can’t be laid at the feet of Jim Hiller alone, particularly when the organization has long-standing questions about consistency and expectations in the postseason.The franchise has been grappling with persistent questions about its ability to convert individual talent into consistent team success. But even with proven performers like Auston Matthews, strong offensive output has not always been enough to overcome defensive gaffes and inconsistent results.Now it’s about improving performances, not letting speculation about the coaching position take over the conversation.The team has to be a little more disciplined with the puck; we have to play a better defensive game, and we have to have a better connection between the forwards and the defence.At this point in time, there’s no reporting to suggest that Hiller is facing imminent dismissal. The Toronto Maple Leafs’ on-ice issues need to be addressed before the conversation around their coaching staff becomes an even bigger distraction.

Article Title: First-ball duck! Mahfijul Islam suffers Test debut nightmare as Kagiso Rabada scripts rare bowling record
Article Text:
South Africa's Kagiso Rabada celebrates after taking the wicket of Bangladesh's Mahfijul Islam. (AP Photos)

Rabada joins elite South African list

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh collapse after early Rabada strikes

Bangladesh debutant Mahfijul Islam endured a nightmare start to his Test career, while South Africa speedster Kagiso Rabada etched his name into the record books with a rare first-ball dismissal in the opening Test at the Wanderers Stadium on Sunday.Mahfijul was dismissed for a golden duck off the very first legal delivery of the match, becoming the first Bangladesh batter and only the fourth player in Test history to be dismissed off the opening ball of a Test on debut.The left-handed batter, drafted into the playing XI as a replacement for the injured Shadman Islam, edged a delivery from Rabada that seamed away and was caught in the slips. His dismissal handed Rabada an immediate breakthrough and left Bangladesh reeling at the start of their innings.The unwanted record had previously been registered by South Africa's Jimmy Cook, who fell to Kapil Dev in Durban in 1992, West Indies' Leon Garrick, dismissed by Allan Donald in Kingston in 2001, and Afghanistan's Abdul Malik, who was dismissed by Blessing Muzarabani in Abu Dhabi in 2019.While Mahfijul's dismissal marked a forgettable beginning to his international career, Rabada's first-ball breakthrough brought him a place in an exclusive group of South African bowlers.He became only the fourth South African to take a wicket with the first legal delivery of a men's Test match, joining Bert Vogler, Allan Donald and Dale Steyn.Vogler was the first to achieve the feat, dismissing England's Tom Hayward with the opening delivery of the Oval Test in 1907. Donald followed suit when he removed Garrick in the Kingston Test in 2001.Steyn then joined the list in 2010, dismissing England opener Andrew Strauss with the first ball of a Test match. Rabada has now become the latest Proteas fast bowler to achieve the distinction.The early breakthrough was the beginning of a difficult opening session for Bangladesh, who opted to bat after winning the toss.Rabada struck again almost immediately, dismissing Mominul Haque for a duck to leave the visitors at 2/2. He then removed Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto in the ninth over, reducing them to 22/3 and putting South Africa firmly in control.Bangladesh were chasing their first-ever Test victory over South Africa. They had lost 14 of their previous 16 meetings, with the remaining two ending in draws.
Article Summary: Mahfijul Islam becomes only fourth player in Test history to be dismissed off the opening ball of a Test on debut. South Africa fast bowler Rabada becomes the fourth South African to take a wicket with the first legal delivery of a men's Test match. Bert Vogler, Allan Donald and Dale Steyn have also achieved the distinction.

The dhol beats synced with Arshdeep Singh 's run-up as he steamed in to bowl the final over his spell. India were three wickets away from a win, and Shreyas Iyer rolled the dice hoping to pick a crucial wicket. Two steps in, both Arshdeep and the dhol missed their beat, forcing the left-arm bowler to abort his run-up and restart. He returned to the top of his mark and did exactly what was expected: pick a wicket and keep the visitors in striking distance of a famous win.With eight wickets down, India had their tails up and both the DJ and crowd joined in to lift the mood at the Bay Oval. The hands which were earlier warming inside the pockets were now applauding the bowling attack for its lion-hearted performance. The equation was delicately placed at 37 runs needed off 30 balls when Iyer turned to Mohammed Siraj , bowling his final over, in search of the last two wickets. Only Yash Thakur 's one over and spin bowling remained for the last four wickets, and those were truly the most important six deliveries of the match for India.He nearly got the job done but Ishan Kishan misjudged an edge behind the stumps and the ball raced to the boundary. The frustration was evident in the Indian camp, as the majority of the remaining bowling would be spin. Then Axar Patel came in and struck on the second delivery, leaving India just one wicket away from a hard-fought win. New Zealand survived Yash Thakur's final over but Axar picked the final wicket to help India register a 22-run win.Not just in this game but the entire series, especially in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah , Prasidh Krishna , Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi, Mohammed Siraj and Yash Thakur stepped up, receiving able support from the spin of Axar Patel and Naman Dhir.Defending a 210-run target, the focus was never on saving runs but on pressing for ten wickets. Iyer attacked with his wicket-taking options, even if it meant bowling out Arshdeep in the 43rd over and introducing spin for the first time in the 36th over of New Zealand's innings.Much like the fourth ODI, the golden hour injected fresh life into the surface and India exerted enough pressure by picking wickets at regular intervals. The tight lines ensured the run-rate was never in comfortable territory during the run-chase. It was a good old-fashioned ODI fixture but both teams had their moments and momentum kept shifting either way.But the evening breeze and the relentlessness of the inexperienced bowling attack plastered over the batting cracks, helping India stage an emphatic fight, seal the series 3-1 and complete the white-ball leg with two trophies in the cabinet.India 209 in 42.1 overs (Axar Patel 46, Ishan Kishan 46; Mitchell Santner 3/47, Jacob Duffy 3/60) beat New Zealand 187 in 48.1 overs (Dean Foxcroft 31; Arshdeep Singh 3/30) by 22 runs.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by 22 runs to clinch ODI series 3-1. India bowled New Zealand out for 210 in their innings. New Zealand were bowled out for 187 in their 50 overs. Shreyas Iyer took three wickets and Axar Patel took the other two.

The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on Sunday. The dates and fixtures of the tournament will remain unchanged.The fifth edition of the WPL will be played from January 14 to February 7, with Vadodara and Mumbai serving as the two host cities. The first leg will take place at the BCA Stadium in Vadodara from January 14 to 24, while Mumbai will host the remaining matches from January 26 until the final on February 7.The Mumbai leg was originally scheduled to be held at the Cricket Club of India’s (CCI) Brabourne Stadium. However, the venue has been changed as CCI is also set to host the inaugural edition of the ICC Women's Champions Trophy in the T20 format, which begins on February 14. The BCCI said the gap between the two tournaments would not give the pitches enough time to recover.“The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced that the Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League 2027 will now be held at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, instead of the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India (CCI). The dates and fixtures will remain unchanged,” the BCCI said in a statement.“The WPL Governing Council approved the original venues and dates for the fifth edition of the TATA WPL at its meeting on 15 September 2026.Under the approved schedule, the Mumbai leg, comprising Match Nos. 12 to 20, the Eliminator and the Final, was to be played at CCI between 26 January and 7 February 2027.”“As CCI is also scheduled to host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, commencing on 14 February, the interval between the conclusion of the TATA WPL and the start of the multi-nation tournament would not provide sufficient time for the pitches to recover,” the board added.The BCCI said the venue was changed following a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC). The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg.“The change follows a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC) to shift the matches scheduled to be played at CCI. The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium now set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg,” the BCCI said.The Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA), during its 95th Annual General Meeting, had formally requested the BCCI to consider it for hosting matches in case of changes to the schedules of future series.

Article Title: UP polls: Congress has asked for 181 seats, Akhilesh reveals for first time
Article Text:

LUCKNOW: As an alliance partner of Samajwadi Party in the INDIA bloc, the Congress wants to contest on 181 seats in UP. This was formally confirmed for the first time by SP president Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday. The confirmation came moments after Akhilesh said that INDIA bloc will defeat BJP in UP polls and ruled out any change in alliance’s constituents in the future and added that SP has decided how many seats SP will contest.Until now, Congress leadership has been throwing numbers in media interviews -- demanding equal partner status in UP polls and suggesting that it wants to contest on half of the 403 Assembly seats. The SP leadership, however, has been clear on its stance that winnability of candidates will remain the sole criterion for fielding candidates rather than count of seats. It has insisted that the priority id to defeat the BJP.Also read | 'Many visitors appear during election season': Akhilesh plays down Owaisi-Azad alliance ahead of UP polls As INDIA bloc members, SP and Congress had outperformed the BJP in 2024 Lok Sabha polls by winning 43 of the 80 seats in UP and getting 43.52% of the votes. Congress had bagged six of the 17 seats it contested with a vote share of 9.46%, while SP had its best-ever winning tally of 37 seats. The BJP’s seats fell from 62 in 2019 to 33 and lowered its overall tally below the majority mark in the Lok Sabha for the first time since 2014.The Congress contested the 2022 UP polls on its own but won just two seats, down by five seats from its tally of 7 in 2017 polls. Of the 399 seats that Congress contested in 2022, it secured a vote share of 2.33% (21.51 lakh votes). Not surprisingly, of the 399 seats, Congress candidates lost their deposits on 387 seats. On 46 seats the party got 10,000 plus votes. Of these 46 seats, 10 of them have sitting SP MLAs. The SP had won 111 seats in 2022.On Saturday, Akhilesh was responding to questions at HT Leadership Summit in Delhi when he emphasised that SP enjoys “very good” relationship with the Congress. Asked that Congress was seeking to contest 100 seats in UP polls, he said: “The number of seats they have asked for is higher than what you are suggesting.” Asked whether the Congress has demanded 200 seats, Akhilesh said the count was slightly less. “Add one to 180,” the SP chief said when asked if the Congress had sought 180 seats.Talking of his experiences with the alliances that he had entered in the past and if he had explored possibilities of reviving 2019 Lok Sabha poll alliance with Bahujan Samaj Party, Akhilesh said he had had good experiences with the alliances. He said his present alliance (with the Cong) stood on the movement and principles of Baba Saheb Ambedkar that was initiated by the BSP.“The INDIA bloc alliance with the Congress that we have had in the past (2024 Lok Sabha polls), is the same alliance that we have today. I don’t see any change in that,” Akhilesh said. On the issue of delay in finalising seat sharing with the Congress, Akhilesh said Samajwadi Party and he has decided on how many seats they will contest. This time SP is going to defeat BJP. INDIA bloc together will defeat BJP,’ Akhilesh said, confirming that Congress has sought 181 seats.
Article Summary: As an alliance partner of Samajwadi Party in the INDIA bloc, the Congress wants to contest on 181 seats in UP. This was formally confirmed for the first time by SP president Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday. The confirmation came moments after AkHilesh said that INDia bloc will defeat BJP in UP polls. Until now, Congress leadership has been throwing numbers in media interviews.

When my brother was alive, there were talks on a merger and a date had been fixed. The day he passed away -- in my mind and within our party -- there was a full-stop to this,” she said.She clarified that she had not received any proposal regarding the merger from the NCP. “I have not received any proposal by phone, WhatsApp, letter or any other means of communication,” she said.Responding to media questions on whether the NCP (SP) is considering joining the NDA alliance, she said, “There are no such talks. A full-stop can be spoken of only if talks are on.”Regarding her meetings with NCP leader Praful Patel in recent days, she said the two families have known each other for decades and that both of them were part of several parliamentary committees.“We meet regularly in the parliamentary committee on finance and FCRA. He was among the invitees for my daughter’s wedding,” said Sule.When asked about her response to Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sanjay Raut ’s comment that talk of the merger was a myth and would fade in the next two days, she said, “He is like an elder brother to me and a senior leader in the MVA alliance. He has the right to say what he wants.”On the NCP (SP)’s possible support for the Centre’s delimitation bill, Sule said, “Six months ago, they had discussed this with several leaders of the INDIA bloc including me and Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Arvind Sawant. We felt that if the seats in all parliamentary constituencies uniformly rise by 50%, then there is no harm discussing this. The size of the electorate in each parliamentary constituency has risen from 13-14 lakh to 25-30 lakh and it is difficult for MPs to reach out to the entire constituency,” she saidHowever, she added, “There is no proposal before us at the moment. Nor have we seen the bill.”
Article Summary: Supriya Sule categorically ruled out the possibility of the merger of the two NCP parties. She reiterated that this issue had reached a full stop the day her cousin, former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar, was killed in an air crash this Jan.

Article Title: IIT-Bombay students call off 57-day sit-in, will continue dialogue with authorities
Article Text:
IIT Bombay students concluded their 57-day sit-in protest after recovering most of their confiscated belongings.

What Changed After 57 Days of Protest?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: After close to two months of agitation, IIT Bombay students have called off their sit-in protest following the return of belongings seized during a police intervention on campus last month. The decision came after talks with the Dean of Student Affairs and an email from institute director prof Shireesh Kedare outlining measures towards systemic reforms. It also coincides with the institute’s end semester exam which began on Nov 10.The protesting students, who had regrouped under Justice Corner 2.0, called it a victory for campus democracy. However, a laptop belonging to one student remains with the authorities, they claimed.The confrontation began on Sept 18 after the death by suicide of second year student Sahil Wakode.In an email to students on Friday, prof Kedare detailed initiatives undertaken over the semester, particularly the preceding two months, to address concerns raised by students and campus stakeholders.These included strengthening mental health support, reviewing hostel rules, improving grievance redressal mechanisms, expanding recreational facilities and upgrading campus infrastructure.Student representatives, faculty, alumni and administrators were working together on these initiatives, he said.“Meaningful institutional reform is a long-term effort,” Kedare wrote, stressing the need for patience, consistency and sustained engagement. He said the institute aimed to build systems that were more responsive to students, faculty and staff.The breakthrough followed a meeting with the Dean of Student Affairs. In a social media post, the Justice Corner collective said the administration had acknowledged several lapses in existing systems and assured students that their demands were being addressed.“We’ll hold them to it. Justice Corner will keep watch, follow up, and make sure every promise turns into action,” the collective said.The students, however, maintained that the return of their belongings was secured through collective pressure rather than administrative goodwill.“We are calling off our protest today; we have almost all of our confiscated belongings back. We received an email from the Director regarding our demands and future dialogue,” the collective announced, calling for a victory march at 9.30 pm on Friday.While the immediate standoff has ended, all eyes are on the police report and the findings of the enquiry committee set up by the IITB board of governors.The students have made clear that the protest’s withdrawal does not mean an end to their campaign. “We will continue fighting against every injustice,” they said.The 57-day student protest following Sahil Wakode’s death on September 18 has prompted several commitments and changes at IIT Bombay.On paper:- 18 demands: Director signed the students’ charter on September 20.- Mental health: 30 new counsellor posts announced.- Review committees: Panels constituted to examine the SC/ST Cell, hostel conditions and mental health concerns.- Examination rules: Revision underway to ensure students accused of violations can present their defence.On campus:- Student feedback: Regular surveys introduced to assess campus concerns.- Greater dialogue: Student bodies presenting reports at General Body Meetings; departmental open houses held or planned.- Communication: More direct administrative engagement on mental health, discrimination and student rights.- Everyday changes: Revised delivery timings and reportedly more responsive faculty and administrators.Still unresolved:- Release of the internal report on Sahil’s death.- Independent inquiry into the incident.- Safeguards for students facing disciplinary accusations.The sit-in has ended, but implementation remains the test.
Article Summary: The confrontation began on Sept 18 after the death by suicide of second year student Sahil Wakode. The decision came after talks with the Dean of Student Affairs and an email from institute director prof Shireesh Kedare outlining measures towards systemic reforms. However, a laptop belonging to one student remains with the authorities.

Article Title: Late drama in Bengaluru as Hannan salvages a point against Real Kashmir
Article Text:
In a thrilling Indian Football League match, FC Bengaluru United faced Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





BENGALURU: There was late drama in the Indian Football League clash between FC Bengaluru United and Real Kashmir FC at the Bangalore Football Stadium here on Saturday. The visitors, leading 2-1, were sniffing victory, but Abdul Hannan had some other plans. The FCBU defender scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute.The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but FCBU goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save to salvage a point with a 2-2 draw for the home team.It was RKFC who looked in control during the initial exchanges. They used both the flanks effectively and made their possession count as forward Zahir Khan met Lalawmpuia Sailo’s cross to head into the empty net and take the lead in the 11th minute. However, FCBU regrouped after conceding the goal, and their efforts bore fruit ten minutes later.Colombian Maikol Andres Herrera fancied his chances from 25-odd yards. The long-ranger was out of the reach of Real Kashmir’s diving goalkeeper Susnata Malik to make it all square with a wonder strike into the top bin.It did not take long for the visitors to regain the lead with defender Shanid Valan scoring an outrageous goal.A miskick from midfielder Rohen Singh reached Valan inside the box, and he backheeled the ball above the goalkeeper to stun FCBU players in the 29th minute. Ribhav Sardesai then came close to making it all square, but his curling effort struck the crossbar.At the other end, FCBU defenders also made some last-minute tackles to keep the score 1-2 at the break. RKFC dominated possession for most of the second half, with FCBU being tactically outsmarted. Despite the dominance, they failed to find the net, though they came close with Amzard Khan striking the crossbar. But in the end, it was Hannan who emerged the hero as his late header helped FCBU snatch a draw.
Article Summary: FC Bengaluru United drew 2-2 with Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore Football Stadium. Abdul Hannan scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute. The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save.

Article Title: Canadian woman travels to Rajasthan to marry man she met on dating app; he backs out after discovering she is 61
Article Text:
The woman arrived in Delhi on November 11 on a tourist visa.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





NEEMRANA: A Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app.However, the man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age. Following a dispute between the two, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.The incident took place in Neemrana in Rajasthan's Behror district. Police reached the spot around 4am on November 13 after receiving information from the Canadian embassy. They took the woman and the man to the police station for questioning.According to Neemrana SHO Surendra Yadav, Nitin, a resident of Panipat in Haryana and son of Satyanarayan, had started communicating with the Canadian woman through a dating app around a year ago. Their friendship gradually developed into a relationship, and the two agreed to get married.The woman arrived in Delhi on November 11 on a tourist visa. Nitin went to the airport to receive her and brought her to a flat belonging to his maternal uncle and aunt in the BB Builders Society in Neemrana.The woman reportedly stayed with Nitin at the society for two days. However, when discussions about marriage progressed, Nitin allegedly backed out after learning that the woman was around 61 years old.This led to an argument between the two.On November 13, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy and informed officials about the developments. Following the embassy's communication, Neemrana police reached the society and took both of them to the police station.While police are questioning Nitin, the Canadian woman has been shifted to a care centre in Kotputli. Police are also making arrangements for her return to Canada.Nitin is reportedly employed as a teacher at a private school in Panipat. Further investigation into the matter is underway.
Article Summary: Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app. The man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age. Following a dispute between the two, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.

Article Title: Delhi Moti Nagar murder: Man suspected of murdering 18-year-old woman apprehended
Article Text:
A 29-year-old suspect named Suraj has been apprehended concerning the murder of an 18-year-old saleswoman named Shabnam (Photo credit: X)

What happened inside the showroom?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Police probe and investigation





NEW DELHI: The 29-year-old suspect in the murder of an 18-year-old saleswoman inside a clothing showroom’s trial room in west Delhi’s Moti Nagar has been apprehended.The victim, identified as Shabnam, was found dead inside the trial room of Vastr Mahal on Saturday evening.The suspect, identified as Suraj, is a resident of Sudamapuri in Moti Nagar. Shabnam worked at a showroom near Moti Nagar Metro Station and lived with her family in West Delhi.According to the preliminary investigation, Suraj allegedly knew Shabnam and had been on friendly terms with her earlier. Police suspect that strained personal relations may have led to the murder.Shabnam was allegedly attacked with a sharp-edged weapon inside the trial room. Her body was discovered by showroom employees on Saturday, when they were preparing to close the establishment.Police found a sharp injury on her neck, and a blood-stained knife was recovered near her body.A woman who claimed to have witnessed the events leading to the discovery of the body said Shabnam had previously worked for her before joining a shop directly opposite her workplace.The woman said she had seen Shabnam sitting at the showroom and using her phone around 6.45pm.At around 7.30pm, she received a call from Shabnam’s employer, who informed her that the young woman was missing after a man allegedly assaulted her.The witness said she went to the showroom but could not find Shabnam. Two neighbours later returned after checking CCTV footage and suspecting that she might still be inside the premises.The group entered the showroom and noticed Shabnam’s scarf near the trial room. They then spotted blood coming from inside and alerted the police and her parents.A PCR call reporting a woman lying unconscious inside the showroom was received at Moti Nagar police station on Saturday. A police team reached the spot and found Shabnam dead.Crime team personnel and forensic science laboratory experts inspected the scene and collected evidence. Her body was shifted to the mortuary of Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for a post-mortem examination.During the preliminary investigation, police found that two of the suspect’s brothers are married to two sisters of the deceased.Based on a complaint lodged by Shabnam’s brother, police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Investigators are probing the motive behind the murder.
Article Summary: The victim, identified as Shabnam, was found dead inside the trial room of Vastr Mahal on Saturday evening. Police found a sharp injury on her neck, and a blood- stained knife was recovered near her body. A 29-year-old suspect named Suraj has been apprehended. Police suspect that strained personal relations may have led to the murder.

Article Title: Married UP sub-inspector dies by suicide; woman accused of blackmail arrested for abetment
Article Text:
Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





VARANASI: A 2023-batch police sub-inspector, Sandeep Kumar , 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district.Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him.Ballia SP Iraj Raja on Sunday said that following collection of evidences and lodging of a complaint by Kumar's wife the accused woman Roli Gond was arrested from an orchard near the railway station on the charges of abetment of suicide.Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.Earlier, the incident came to light when a train’s loco pilot informed the Chitbaragaon station master through a memo that someone had jumped before his moving train to commit suicide.On being alerted by railway officials Chitbadagaon police and GRP reached the spot, where Kumar's motorbike and mobile phone were found lying near the railway track while his mutilated body was detected on tracks.On getting information Raja, ASP South Sanjay Verma, CO Akshay Kumar and railway police officials also reached there while forensic team was engaged to collect evidence from the railway track area.Kumar, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was married and had a six-month-old child. He had been posted at Chitbaragaon police station for past 11 months.He was transferred to Pakri police station but had not yet been relieved from his old posting because of Chhath festival arrangements. On Saturday evening, he had left police station by informing colleagues that he was going to his duty point.After postmortem examination the mortal remain of Kumar was brought to the police lines, where following guard of honours officials paid tributes and observed silence for two minutes.The officials also consoled Kumar's family, which also remained at police lines.
Article Summary: Sandeep Kumar, 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district. Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him. Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.

Article Title: 'What difference does it make?': Molester asked Mumbai woman before pushing her off platform; how Naigaon horror unfolded inside local train
Article Text:
A 20-year-old woman confronted a 53-year-old man for alleged molestation inside a Mumbai local train.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





VASAI: “What difference does it make?” was the response a 53-year-old man allegedly gave a 20-year-old woman when she confronted him for molesting her inside a Mumbai local train The exchange soon escalated into a physical altercation at Naigaon station, where the man allegedly pushed her onto the tracks. As she tried to climb back onto the platform, the train began moving, crushing her left arm below the elbow.The woman, who got married just five months ago, had gone to Malad on November 4 to buy a phone. With trains packed, she travelled to Borivli and boarded a Virar-bound slow local. She mistakenly entered the compartment reserved for persons with disabilities.According to her complaint, a man later identified as Jitendra Hirmukhe (53) repeatedly pushed against her inside the crowded compartment. Initially, she ignored him, but when the train reached Bhayander, he allegedly began touching her inappropriately.Both got off at Naigaon station around 7.15pm, where the woman confronted Hirmukhe. Instead of backing off, he allegedly touched her inappropriately again and asked her, “What difference does it make?”Angered by his response, the woman took off her slipper and threw it at him. Hirmukhe allegedly abused her, removed his own slipper and hit her with it.The train was still standing at the platform, and several passengers gathered as the confrontation escalated. Hirmukhe allegedly pushed the woman, causing her to fall onto the tracks into the gap between two coaches.As she tried to climb back onto the platform, the train started moving. She fell into the platform gap, and her left arm came under the train's wheels. The arm was severed below the elbow.Hirmukhe fled the spot. The woman was initially taken to a hospital in Vasai and later shifted to a Mumbai hospital for further treatment. She is undergoing treatment at a civic hospital.Bhayander railway police examined CCTV footage from the station and traced Hirmukhe to his residence in Wakipada, Naigaon East. He was arrested on November 9, five days after the incident. He originally hails from Dharashiv district.“He has stomach cancer and was travelling in the compartment reserved for persons with disabilities. We traced him with the help of CCTV footage and arrested him from Naigaon,” said Ganpat Tumbada, senior inspector, Bhayander railway police.Police initially registered a case under sections 74 ( molestation ), 117(2) (voluntarily causing hurt) and 352 (intentional insult) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Section 109 (attempt to murder) was subsequently added. Hirmukhe is in judicial custody.The woman has demanded the strictest punishment for the accused. “Despite having done nothing wrong, I had to go through this ordeal. I have permanently lost one of my arms... I want justice,” she said in her statement.
Article Summary: Jitendra Hirmukhe, 53, allegedly molested a 20-year-old woman inside a Mumbai local train. The exchange soon escalated into a physical altercation at Naigaon station, where the man allegedly pushed her onto the tracks. As she tried to climb back onto the platform, the train began moving, crushing her left arm below the elbow. The woman was initially taken to a hospital in Vasai and later shifted to a Mumbai hospital.

Article Title: Another setback for AAP in Punjab: Sukhdeep Singh Chhina resigns from posts, primary membership
Article Text:
Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, who served as the Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, has officially stepped down from all roles within the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AAP faces a series of exits in Punjab





CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has suffered another exit in Punjab , with Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, resigning from all party positions and the party's primary membership.Chhina submitted his resignation to AAP Punjab president Aman Arora, formally announcing his decision to sever ties with the party.In his resignation letter addressed to Arora, Chhina wrote: "I, Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, hereby tender my resignation from all positions held in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and also relinquish my primary membership of the party."The letter does not specify a reason for his decision. Chhina has announced his resignation from party positions and primary membership; the statement provided does not mention whether he is also stepping down as Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board.Chhina's resignation comes amid a series of departures from the AAP in Punjab. Earlier this month, two party MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, resigned from the party's primary membership, a day after AAP announced its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.The two resignations came as the party began preparations for the next Assembly polls. AAP has also faced political criticism and dissent from within its Punjab unit in recent weeks.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, who served as the Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, has officially stepped down from all roles within the Aam Aadmi Party. His resignation comes amid a series of departures from the AAP in Punjab. Earlier this month, two party MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra resigned from the party's primary membership.
